No facility ban or presentation offence, but no statewide service protection (roughly 30% municipal coverage), no gender-identity hate-crime coverage, birth certificates retaining original sex, no custody transition care — offsets leave it at parent level.

Shield law, 1993 public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage, open markers, care coverage and most-protective tier lift it well above parent; only documented birth-sex custody placement (2012, dated, resident case) holds it below the top tier.

Facilities access protected by law, public accommodations, hate-crime coverage with a murder conviction, court-ordered care resumption and a 2024 custody consent decree providing remedies; unresolved 2026 ballot measures keep it below the low-risk band.
